newsitem.title: USA: Clinton welcomes Annan, pledges to pay U.S. debt.
newsitem.headline: Clinton welcomes Annan, pledges to pay U.S. debt.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday welcomed new United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan and said he will work with Congress to find a way to pay off the more than $1 billion the United States owes the world body.

"As the U.N. moves to reform, it must know also that the United States is prepared to pay its way," Clinton said after meeting Annan at the White House. "In the weeks ahead I will be working with Congress to reach an agreement in which America can pay our arrears to the U.N.."
"Our (federal) budget will actually have a plan to pay it back, and to pay it back in a prompt fashion," Clinton said.

"As a practical matter I know from consulting with members of Congress that we won't be able to secure support in the Congress for paying the arrears unless they're convinced that reform is going forward."
According to United Nations figures, the United States owes the world body some $1.3 billion.

Annan, who was also meeting with members of Congress during his visit to Washington, emphasised that he too was committed to reforming the United Nations. "I have given my commitment to the president that I will pursue reforms," he said. "If we don't change we may lose our relevance."
